evidence.note: After reading RFC sections, the agent ran test.sh, saw 6/6 pass, and treated that as the completion signal (marked task complete at step 10). No checklist of the feature matrix (frame headers, block types, literals, FSE modes, sequences, dictionaries) — done vs remaining — was ever maintained.

One moment of accurate self-assessment: 'I should not mark the task complete yet. Although the visible tests pass... may fail hidden grading.' Shows awareness that test.sh passing != full coverage, lifting it slightly above pure anchor-3, but this concerns compliance, not feature-coverage tracking.

Repeatedly submits 'complete' based solely on 'builds and passes visible 6 tests,' each time acknowledging the wrapper is non-compliant. Progress is judged by the visible sanity suite, never by which spec features are actually exercised/verified.

Agent abandoned RFC implementation entirely for a libzstd wrapper, so no subsystems existed to track; there is no coverage map and no debugging of real feature classes — the feature matrix is never engaged with.

reasoning: The agent never built or tracked the feature matrix; its progress signal was essentially 'does it build and pass the 6 visible test.sh cases,' which it conflated with a working solution and used as grounds to submit multiple times — squarely anchor-3 behavior. It shows a thin margin above 3 via genuine, repeated awareness that visible tests are not the hidden grading set and that the wrapper is non-compliant, but it keeps no rough checklist of features done vs remaining (anchor 5) and produces no coverage map of any subsystem. Since implementation was abandoned for a wrapper, there is no circular debugging to detect, and no honest map of verified-vs-untested corners of the actual decoder.
